canonical_title: The Minority Report and Other Classic Stories
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Volume 4 of the Collected Stories and a film tie-in edition, headlined by 'The Minority Report,' Dick's 1956 tale of precrime, precognition, and a police chief accused by his own predictive system.
page_summary:
The Minority Report and Other Classic Stories constitutes Volume 4 of The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, gathering work from roughly 1954 to 1964. Its title story, published in 1956, imagines a Precrime division that arrests people for murders they have not yet committed, on the testimony of three precognitive 'precogs' whose visions do not always agree. When the system names its own architect as a future killer, the machinery of prophecy turns on him.

The story became Steven Spielberg's 2002 film and gave this volume its status as a tie-in edition, but it also crystallizes several of Dick's central themes: precognition, the apparatus of a controlling state, and the trap in which a small individual is caught between competing versions of the truth. The 'minority report'—the dissenting vision that reveals the future is not fixed—is one of his purest images of contingency.

The surrounding stories in the volume extend these concerns across time, betrayal, and the suspicion that the visible order conceals another. As a middle volume of the Collected Stories, it captures Dick at the height of his short-form powers.
